name: The Birth of Saint John the Baptist
history: Only three births are kept as feasts in the Church’s calendar: Christ’s, Our Lady’s and John the Baptist’s. John was born to Zechariah and Elizabeth in their old age, sanctified, the Church holds, when he leapt in his mother’s womb at the Visitation. His feast falls six months before Christmas, as the days begin to shorten.
life: Saint Luke tells how the angel Gabriel appeared to the priest Zechariah in the Temple and promised that his wife Elizabeth, long childless, would bear a son. Zechariah doubted and was struck dumb. When Mary, carrying Christ, visited her cousin, the child leapt in Elizabeth’s womb. At his circumcision the neighbours wanted to call him after his father, but Zechariah wrote, ‘His name is John,’ and at once his tongue was loosed and he sang the Benedictus, which the Church prays every morning. John grew up in the desert and came to prepare the way of the Lord, the last of the prophets and the greatest born of women. Saint Augustine saw meaning in the dates: after John’s birth the days grow shorter, after Christ’s they lengthen, for he must increase and I must decrease. The hymn for this feast, Ut queant laxis, gave us the names of the notes of the scale.
prayerTo: Saint John the Baptist, you leapt for joy at the coming of Christ before you were born, and you spent your life pointing to Him. Pray for me, that I may make way for Him in my heart, speak truthfully, and be glad to decrease so that He may increase. Pray for mothers and for children not yet born. Amen.
penance: Pray the Benedictus, Luke 1:68 to 79, this morning or tonight, and make some concrete gift of help to an expectant mother or a pregnancy charity.
meditation: He must increase, but I must decrease. Where do you need to step aside today, so that Christ may be seen?
prayer: O God, Who made this a day most worthy of our celebration because of blessed John; grant Your people the grace of spiritual joys and direct the minds of all the faithful into the path of eternal salvation. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
